title: Laboratory Instructions & Safety
pedagogicalStatus: Unreviewed draft: formative practice only; CEFR mastery disabled.

sources.title: Virtual setup card
paragraphs: This is a computer simulation, not a physical electrical experiment. First, read the setup card on the screen. Next, check the cable symbols in the diagram. Then, ask your instructor if a symbol is unclear. Finally, select Run in the simulation. Do not connect real laboratory equipment during this activity. The screen instructions are for the virtual task only.

sources.title: Teaching-room notice
paragraphs: In this example teaching room, the posted rules say that food and drinks are not allowed at the benches. Students must ask the instructor before using electrical equipment. If a cable looks damaged, do not use it or touch the damaged part; inform the instructor. The instructor decides how to make the area safe. The notice also says students should keep notebooks away from the edges of tables. This last sentence is advice in the example, not the same type of rule as the other instructions.

sources.title: Optics demonstration notice
paragraphs: In the fictional optics demonstration in this lesson, only the instructor operates the laser. Students must not look directly into the beam and must not adjust the laser. They may ask questions from the marked observation area. If a warning indicator appears unexpectedly, students stop participating and inform the instructor. This practice text does not replace local laser-safety training.

sources.title: Warm-surface demonstration
paragraphs: A teacher demonstrates a warm metal plate. First, the teacher checks the equipment and starts the demonstration. Students observe from the marked line. When the display is switched off, students must not assume the plate is cool. They must not touch it unless the instructor explicitly says it is safe. They can write notes or ask for clarification while waiting. Students do not operate this apparatus in the language activity.

items.prompt: Choose the best modal phrase. The example room rule requires an instructor’s approval. Students ___ ask before using a power supply.
items.feedback: A posted requirement takes must; advice takes should.

items.prompt: Choose the best modal phrase. The note suggests keeping writing clear; it is useful advice, not a rule. You ___ label each observation clearly.
items.feedback: Should gives advice here, rather than a requirement.

items.prompt: Choose the best modal phrase. The activity rules require students to read the virtual warning first. They ___ read it before clicking Start.
items.feedback: Have to expresses a rule imposed by the activity.

items.prompt: Choose the best modal phrase. It is optional to write a title in this short practice note. You ___ write a title.
items.feedback: Do not have to means optional; must not means prohibited.

items.prompt: Choose the best modal phrase. The sample room prohibits food at the bench. You ___ bring food to the bench.
items.feedback: Must not means prohibited, not optional.

items.prompt: Choose the best modal phrase. The instructor recommends writing short notes. You ___ write short notes.
items.feedback: Should expresses a recommendation.

items.prompt: Choose the best modal phrase. This model exercise requires checking the on-screen diagram before Run. You ___ check it first.
items.feedback: Must expresses a necessary action in this task.

items.prompt: Choose the best modal phrase. The instructor says a blue pen is not required. Students ___ use a blue pen.
items.feedback: No obligation is not prohibition.
